To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the discrete FRT is defined as the unitary matrix that transforms the eigenvector of the DFT corresponding to a given frequency into a shifted and scaled version of itself, where the shift and scaling parameters depend on the fractional Fourier order.

the DFT has two complete sets of eigenvectors, that one of these sets of eigenvector is the set of Hermie Gaussian functions, and that the discrete FRT is the transform that diagonalizes the DFT in the basis set of these eigenvectors.

the DFT is the fractional Fourier transform of order one and that the DFT can be generalized to the fractional Fourier transform by using the eigenvectors of this transform as a new set of basis functions.

the development and application of a new class of fractional Fourier transform (FRFT).
the definition of the discrete FTR.
developing a theory of fractional transforms for finite dimensional spaces, which will be useful in the analysis of discrete signal processing algorithms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the discrete FRT is the discrete counterpart of FRT, which is a natural extension of the DFT.
the proposed definition of the discrete FTR is the discrete counterpart of that of the continuous FRT.

the definition of the discrete FTR proposed in this paper, which is based on a set of eigenvector of the DFT, is the definitive one, and that it satisfies all the desirable and necessary properties expected of the FRT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have defined the discrete FRT in a manner which is analogous to the definition of the continuous FRT, we have derived the discrete FRT's matrix elements, we have derived its eigenvalues and eigenvectors, we have developed the theory of fractional DFTs, and we have shown the connection between the continuous and discrete fractional FRTs.
this definition of the discrete FTR provides a unified and complete framework for the analysis of linear systems in both time and frequency domains.

we have provided a complete mathematical description of the discrete FFR and its properties, which includes its eigenfunctions, its eigenvectors, its matrix representation, its relationship to the discrete Hartley Transform (DHT), its relationship to the DFT, its properties and applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the discrete FRT is the discrete counterpart of its continuous version, and not the DFT raised to an arbitrary power.
the discrete FRT is a unitary transform which is not a simple power of the DFT, and that it can be computed by means of the discrete sine transform.
the DFT can be seen as the special case of the discrete FTR when the fractional order is an integer multiple of 1/N, where N is the number of points in the DFT.
